details: A postinstall script collects PII — hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI identity, current working directory, platform, and architecture — and POSTs it to a Google Cloud Run endpoint. The README claims "anonymous diagnostics" while the script actually transmits email addresses and identity data. This is deceptive install-time identity harvesting. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall script (postinstall.js) harvests hostname, OS username, git email (from ~/.gitconfig), GitHub CLI identity (from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml), current working directory, and CI provider, then POSTs it to a Google Cloud Run endpoint. The README falsely claims only platform, Node version, and architecture are collected. The package ships no working code — its declared main (dist/index.js) is absent — and a bundled publish-versions.sh states it "creates the appearance of an active, maintained package." This is a deceptive install-time identity-harvesting facade.
